tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

2

7	shows every table with its default or a typical value. `vc-x1 config` prints the same schema from
8	the binary you are running.

12	#

14	# relative to this file's directory (absolute allowed, discouraged).

1	# Notes file conventions
2	
3	Conventions the agent follows when reading and writing notes files (`TODO.md`,
4	`notes/todo-backlog.md`, `notes/bugs.md`, and the frozen `notes/chores/chores-NN.md` and
5	`notes/done.md`, [Frozen history](#frozen-history-chores-and-done)). One source of truth lives here,
6	and [`notes/README.md`](../notes/README.md) points back. Read this before editing a notes file.
7	
8	Universal file, shared with the template repository. A proposed change is edited here and converges
9	at the template ([Changing the agent-files](../AGENTS.md#changing-the-agent-files)). Project-local
10	content goes in [custom.md](../custom.md).
11	
12	## File reads: read the slice you need
13	
14	Long notes files are appended to over time. Read only the slice your task needs. Grep or read
15	further on demand ([why](rationale.md#file-reads-read-the-slice-you-need)).
16	
17	- **`TODO.md`** (the routine acquaint read): the first ~60 lines covers intro + `## In Progress` +
18	  the top of `## Todo`, its entries in priority order. `Read` with `offset=0, limit=60`.
19	  `## Ideas` sits below `## Todo`. Read further only when chasing a lower entry, an Idea, a
20	  `[N]` ref, or auditing the whole list.
21	- **`notes/todo-backlog.md`**: the long-tail backlog (lower-priority entries below `## Todo`). Read
22	  only when picking up a backlog item, and grep to locate it first.
23	- **`notes/bugs.md`**: the bug list. Small, so read it whole when triaging a bug or chasing the
24	  `## Bugs` pointer in `TODO.md`.
25	- **`notes/done.md`** + **`notes/chores/chores-NN.md`**: frozen history. Scan headings first
26	  (`grep '^## ' notes/chores/chores-NN.md`), then read only the section you need.
27	
28	## Notes references
29	
30	Reference *citations* are double-bracketed so the brackets render: `[[N]]`, or `[[2]],[[3]]` for
31	several (comma-separated, not `[2,3]` or `[[2]][[3]]`). The `[N]:` definitions in a file's
32	`# References` section and inline `[text](url)` / `[text](#anchor)` links stay single-bracketed.
33	
34	## Reference numbering
35	
36	Every note file keeps a file-local `# References` section at the bottom, and its numbers are scoped
37	to that file: the same `[1]` in two files is two independent slots, each pointing wherever its own
38	file defines.
39	
40	- Treat `[N]` as a **footnote**, a slot meaningful only inside its own file's `# References`, so a
41	  citation never reuses another file's number. To cite a target a sibling file references, take your
42	  own next free slot and define it, and the same target may carry a different number in each file.
43	- A `[N]` *inside a code span* (`` `[72]` ``) is a quoted identifier, data rather than a citation,
44	  so it needs no definition.
45	- To point at a section of another file, use an inline link with an anchor rather than a bare
46	  number.
47	- A definition is usually a path with an anchor, and may also be a **same-file fragment**,
48	  `[N]: #<slug>`, which is how a ladder rung links its own subsection ([The In Progress
49	  block](#the-in-progress-block)).
50	- A file's `# References` may be **re-packed** to a contiguous `[1]..[N]` in first-citation order,
51	  walking the file's prose top to bottom. A file-local rewrite: no other file moves, and a new ref
52	  may take the next free number, out of order being fine. Ask before re-packing, and never re-pack
53	  [frozen history](#frozen-history-chores-and-done).
54	
55	## Markdown anchor links
56	
57	GitHub anchor algorithm: lowercase, strip non-alphanumeric characters in place, map remaining spaces
58	to hyphens 1-for-1. Do **not** collapse adjacent whitespace, so `a + b` -> `a--b` (spaces on both
59	sides of `+`), but `a: b` -> `a-b` (only trailing space on `:`). General markdown reference:
60	[markdownguide.org](https://www.markdownguide.org). GitHub publishes no official spec for
61	auto-generated anchors. The de-facto reference implementation is
62	[github-slugger](https://github.com/Flet/github-slugger).
63	
64	## Todo format
65	
66	`TODO.md` has these sections, in this order. Each item in them is a short description with
67	reference links to more detail.
68	
69	- `## Continuation notes`: where the agent was, for the agent that comes next. Ephemeral, never a
70	  record, `_None._` by default, written before a restart or a loss of context, and reset by the
71	  agent that reads it, after filing each fact into its home or keeping the bullet whose fact has
72	  none, so a reset never destroys the only copy of anything.
73	- `## In Progress`: the running cycle's record ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)).
74	- `## Waiting`: important work that cannot start yet. Each entry names what it waits on and its
75	  rank once unblocked, and every opening checks the conditions.
76	- `## Todo`: entries in priority order, the first highest. The long-tail backlog is in
77	  [todo-backlog.md](../notes/todo-backlog.md).
78	- `## Ideas`: unranked.
79	- `## Bugs`: a pointer to [bugs.md](../notes/bugs.md).
80	- `## Closed`: the last cycle's finished record.
81	- `# References`: the file-local reference definitions, the file's last section ([Reference
82	  numbering](#reference-numbering)).
83	
84	Every adopter has one `TODO.md` of this shape. It is not an agent-file, since its content is the
85	project's record, and the payload ships it as a skeleton: `## In Progress` reading
86	`_No cycle currently in progress._`, the other sections empty.
87	
88	An entry is a `###` heading, its title, followed by its text. Priority is file order, the first
89	entry the highest, and reprioritizing is moving the entry. The title is unique within its file and
90	is the entry's anchor, so a citation is a link, `[title](TODO.md#<slug>)`, that the anchor check
91	verifies ([Prose form](prose.md#prose-form) for the text). Entries carry no number: a rank number
92	renumbers on every move and every citation that holds one goes stale, which is why the numbered
93	form was retired (2026-08-27). An entry's sub-entries, when it groups several, are bullets with a
94	bold title, cited by the bold text.
95	
96	Example shape:
97	
98	```
99	## Todo
100	
101	### Add new feature X
102	
103	The feature, in a sentence or two ([details](features.md#feature-x)).
104	
105	### Fix bug Y
106	
107	What is wrong and where [[1]].
108	
109	[1]: bugs.md#bug-y
110	```
111	
112	## The In Progress block
113	
114	A cycle's record, `TODO.md > ## In Progress`, written at the opening
115	([Opening](../AGENTS.md#opening)), finalized and moved to `## Closed` by the closing commit, and
116	deleted by the next opening ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)). The picked-up `## Todo`
117	item is moved here (never copied) and becomes the cycle-record's **provisional items**, all
118	required, all revised as rungs land. The title is a heading one level below `## In Progress` and the
119	other five are headings one level below the title (a plain cycle: `###` title, `####` items, and
120	under a program heading, each one deeper):
121	
122	- **title**, the cycle's name, what `git log --grep` finds it by
123	- **problem statement**: what is wrong, a sentence or two
124	- **solution statement**: what will be done about it, broad. Provisional, and the close-out's commit
125	  body carries the final one
126	- **acceptance check**: the measure of "are you finished?", specific enough that a reader can run
127	  it. Not the per-commit validation, which asks whether the artifact still works. A changed check is
128	  one of the things the deliberation exists to justify
129	- **deliberation**: how the other five were decided, one bullet per decision. The bullet's lead
130	  names the decision and its sentence states it, and the sub-bullets carry the reasons, the
131	  alternatives weighed, and the costs accepted, so a reader can skim the decisions and read the
132	  reasons only where they doubt one. `_None._` when there was nothing to deliberate, which is a real
133	  answer
134	- **ladder**: one rung per step, `- [<title>][M]` plus `(current)` / `(done)`, with `[M]: #<slug>`
135	  in the file's `# References`. The markers stay when the block moves to `## Closed`. `<title>` is
136	  the rung's commit title, `<type>: <desc>` per
137	  [Conventional-commit shape](prose.md#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit), so a moved
138	  `## Todo` entry is retitled. The closing rung, `<cycle title> closing`, is linked like the rest
139	
140	The ladder heads the **rung subsections**, one per rung under it, the closing included, headed by
141	the rung's exact title, so the ladder is their index. Each opens at laddering with an abstract-sized
142	intent statement (the rung's problem and solution in a sentence or two) and completes at the rung's
143	landing with the conceptual delta: design points, consequences, deferrals, never a restatement of
144	the landed commit body. The closing rung's opens with the stub "Closing out the cycle." and
145	completes at close-out with what closing taught, in problem/solution form, or `_None._`.
146	
147	A rung is `- [<title>][M] (marker)` and carries no detail beyond that: the title links to the rung's
148	subsection. A step is identified by its title (prose.md's [Steps are named, not
149	numbered](prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered)), so a title carries no number, no version, and no
150	SHA. The version-of-record still bumps for every rung and its suffix still encodes the stage, but
151	that encoding belongs to the manifest and appears nowhere in prose.
152	
153	A single-step cycle's ladder is one unlinked rung, `- <cycle title> (marker)`, with no subsection
154	under it: a subsection headed by the title would collide with the title heading's anchor ([Cycle
155	shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)).
156	
157	The block is the cycle's only record. A design finding that must outlive the cycle goes into a
158	`notes/` file by the rung that made it ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)).
159	
160	## Frozen history: chores and done
161	
162	`notes/chores/chores-NN.md` and `notes/done.md` are the records of cycles that ran before the
163	cycle-record became `TODO.md > ## In Progress` alone ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)).
164	They are frozen: nothing is appended, no section is opened, no entry is retired into them, and no
165	ref is backfilled. They stay in place because Todo entries and design notes link into them, and
166	those links stay valid. Read them as history, by the slice you need.
167

completes at close-out with what closing taught, in problem/solution form, or `_None._`.

A rung is `- [<title>][M] (marker)` and carries no detail beyond that: the title links to the rung's
subsection. A step is identified by its title (prose.md's [Steps are named, not
numbered](prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered)), so a title carries no number, no version, and no
SHA. The version-of-record still bumps for every rung and its suffix still encodes the stage, but
that encoding belongs to the manifest and appears nowhere in prose.

A single-step cycle's ladder is one unlinked rung, `- <cycle title> (marker)`, with no subsection
under it: a subsection headed by the title would collide with the title heading's anchor ([Cycle
shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)).

The block is the cycle's only record. A design finding that must outlive the cycle goes into a
`notes/` file by the rung that made it ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)).

## Frozen history: chores and done

`notes/chores/chores-NN.md` and `notes/done.md` are the records of cycles that ran before the
cycle-record became `TODO.md > ## In Progress` alone ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)).
They are frozen: nothing is appended, no section is opened, no entry is retired into them, and no
ref is backfilled. They stay in place because Todo entries and design notes link into them, and
those links stay valid. Read them as history, by the slice you need.

224	- m-41-0 2026-09-09T16:00:00Z from abc to def,ghi hello
225	- m-41-1 2026-09-09T16:05:42Z from ghi to abc hi

237	
238	- one thing
239	- another, with the command that shows it:
240	
241	  ```
242	  vc-x1 validate --fast
243	  ```
244	````

  two clones can mint the same id, a thread's from `threads` or a line's from the same last line.
  The rejected push catches it and the loser renumbers, which is why an id is final only once
  pushed. A second clone that never collides means member-scoped ids for threads and lines both,
  and that is the change it would take.
- No access control. Any member can modify or delete any file here. It works among friendly
  participants, and history is the only recourse.
- No commit per line. Under one clone the mutex is what keeps writes from interleaving, and a
  line's author and time are in the line, so a commit adds only the link to the session that
  wrote it. Committing batches lines, pushing backs them up, and the version commit is the one
  commit the rules require.
- No archive. `closed/` grows by a file per thread and its bodies, and git and `rg` carry that
  far past this family's traffic. The technique comes when it matters, a directory per year or a
  store outside the tree, and the ids, never reused, survive either.

## Versions

The title carries the rules' version, and the tree is always at that version: the commit that
bumps it edits this file and rewrites `open/` and `closed/` to the new shape in the same commit,
under the mutex, with every member's last push already in `main@origin`. History is never
rewritten, so a reader supports one shape, the one this file describes, and a tool that finds
the title behind it says so rather than parsing the past.

- v0.3.3: a commit is titled with the ids of the threads it touches, `m-3 m-4`, a close
  included, so the close form and the line-id form go. The first batch under v0.3.2 carried five
  lines across two threads and five ids read as noise, and a commit that closed two threads had
  no title form, iiac-perf's finding at `m-3-1`. The title is a convenience, never a store, and
  the diff says what the commit did in each thread.
- v0.3.2: a commit that closes a thread is titled `close m-<tid> <title>` whatever lines it
  carries, and a title that lists ids is for a batch that closes nothing. The first close under
  v0.3.1, `13a7d9f7`, carried six lines, and six ids read as noise where the close is the event.
- v0.3.1: no blank line under the heading, so line `<num>` is file line `<num>` plus two, closed
  threads move to `closed/` instead of being deleted, a commit may carry any number of actions,
  the close in the same commit as its last `done`, and a release may leave lines uncommitted, so
  the clean-working-copy guard is gone and a commit batches whatever the working copy holds. A
  member's own line, of either action, clears what was pending for them, so a reply needs no
  `done` after it, `done` is the empty reply, and `read` is retired, since a line that clears
  nothing has no place in a query over lines. From the `m-2` replies: addressed means the
  recipient field alone, a reply answers everything it clears, naming each, and `owner`'s times
  are UTC to the second. The migration restored `m-1` from history without its blank line, its
  surplus `done` marks still valid lines.
- v0.3.0, the cutover from v0.2.0's records and inboxes: every record was complete, so no
  thread carried over. `threads` was created at 0, `notices.md`, `topics/`, the inboxes,
  `README-old.md`, and the `.owner` copy of the mutex were deleted, and the draft became this
  file. The v0.2.0 tree is the tag `v0.2.0`, and `git log -S'<heading>'` finds a record.

Acquainted. This is a fresh workspace with no cycle running, nothing pending for us in messages, and one Todo entry ready to open.

## State

- **Work-repo**: `main` is at `Initial commit` (602cb677). The working copy on top of it is undescribed and holds the whole agent-files set (v0.2.6), `TODO.md`, `README.md`, `custom.md` and the licenses. There is no cycle bookmark, and no Cargo project or `notes/` directory yet.
- **Agent-repo** (`.agent-session`): `main` is at `Initial commit`, and its working copy is empty.
- **Continuation notes**: there are none to act on. The section holds only its description, without the `_None._` marker.
- **Todo**: the one entry is "Read bytes from linux keyboard via io_uring". It asks for an app that uses zc-ring-x1 mpsc and/or spsc v4 to receive keyboard bytes as typed and echo them, with CR echoing CRLF and Ctrl+q quitting. `## Waiting` is empty.
- **Messages** (`../vc-x1-messages`, v0.3.3): nothing is addressed to us, and the clone is free (last line is `release iiac-perf`). The one open thread, m-7, is between iiac-perf and zc-ring-x1. It matters to the Todo because it describes the current spsc v4 role API:
  - `claim_producer(id)` and `claim_consumer(id)` replace `producer()` and `consumer()`.
  - There is no `split`, and no `Drop` release.
  - `release()` and `take_over_*` sit beside the claims.

## Things I noticed

- **Stray ladder**: `## In Progress` reads `_No cycle currently in progress._` but is followed by a `### Ladder` with `- feat: default to .agent-session (done)`. It looks like a leftover from the template.
- **Missing sections**: `TODO.md` has no `## Ideas`, `## Bugs` or `## Closed`, and it links `notes/todo-backlog.md`, which does not exist.
- **No `[validate]` table**: `.vc-config.md` has none, so `vc-x1 validate` has nothing project-specific to run until there is a crate.
- **Member name**: the name differs across the directory (`io_uring-2-zcr-v4-x1`), the agent-repo remote (`io_uring-2-zcr-v4.agent-session`) and the README title (`io_uring_2_zcr-v4`). The messages README names a member by its project's name, so I need to know which one is ours before I write there.
- **Fetch**: the messages protocol suggests considering a fetch when nothing is pending and the clone is free. I did not fetch, since that needs your go.

I changed nothing. Tell me whether to open the keyboard cycle or tidy `TODO.md` first.

# Todo and cycle record

This file contains near term tasks with a short description and reference links to more details.
Its shape is [Todo format](agent-data/notes.md#todo-format).

## Continuation notes

Where the agent was, for the agent that comes next: working copy state, the step in flight, an
open question. Ephemeral, never a record. Written before a restart or when a session is about to
lose context, read first at acquaint, acted on, and reset to `_None._` by the reader.

_None._

## In Progress

A cycle's record has one home at a time, and while the cycle runs this is it. The block's
shape is the specimen in [cycle-model.md](agent-data/cycle-model.md), and the rules are in
[The In Progress block](agent-data/notes.md#the-in-progress-block).

_No cycle currently in progress._

## Closed

The last cycle's finished record, moved here whole by its closing commit and deleted by the next
opening ([Cycle-record](AGENTS.md#cycle-record)).

## Waiting

Important work that cannot start yet. Each entry names what it waits on, in a form that can be
checked, and the rank it takes in `## Todo` once unblocked. Every opening checks each condition
and promotes what is met ([Opening](AGENTS.md#opening)).

## Todo

Entries are in priority order, the first highest, and reprioritizing is moving an entry. Each is a
`###` heading, so a citation is a link to its anchor. Long-tail entries live in
[todo-backlog.md](notes/todo-backlog.md). Use the [Prose form](agent-data/prose.md#prose-form).
Deeper detail goes in a `notes/` design file (link via `[N]` ref).

## Ideas

Items not yet solid enough for `## Todo` (or surfaced during close-out / end-of-day before they
are fully formed). Triaged at the next opening: promote to `## Todo` /
[todo-backlog.md](notes/todo-backlog.md), fold into a picked-up cycle, or drop.

## Bugs

_See [bugs.md](notes/bugs.md)._

renumber.

# Notes

This directory holds the project's records: chores, bugs, the long-tail backlog, and topic
files, each organized for easy reference. Records only; universal rules live in
`../agent-data/` (see [../AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md)'s file map).

By default there are the chores-NN.md files in [chores/](chores). Chores are general notes
about tasks; short-term tasks and their status live at the repo root in
[../TODO.md](../TODO.md). The chores-NN files are numbered in sequence; the highest-numbered
file is the active one, older ones are closed.

Multi-cycle programs too big for a TODO.md entry get their own dated plan file here: one `##`
section per stage, so chores and todo entries can reference a stage by anchor. The plan file
owns the forward design; chores still records each shipped cycle.

A rule that governs what the artifact does, rather than a record of what was done, gets its
own topic file so it can be found without knowing which cycle produced it. The investigation
behind such a rule stays where it happened (a plan file or a chores section) and is linked
from the policy, so neither restates the other.

Example chores file:

```
# Chores-01.md

General maintenance tasks and considerations for the project see other files for
more specific topics. A chore in a chores file provides quick information on the
how and why of a particular chore.

## Create a binary that lists jj info

This binary should list the changeID, commitID, and description title
and using `jj-lib`
```

## Workflow and conventions

Bot-facing workflow and conventions live in [`../AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md) (hard rules + file
map) and its `../agent-data/` satellites:

- [Notes file conventions](../agent-data/notes.md): Todo format, Reference numbering, Notes
  references (`[[N]]` citation style), Markdown anchor links, Retiring Done entries, Chores
  conventions (section headers / Done entries exact-title rule, content rules, the as-built
  ladder and its commit reference format, the chores Table of Contents).
- [Prose and durable text](../agent-data/prose.md): prose form, typeable punctuation,
  conventional-commit shape.
- [Code conventions](../agent-data/code.md): doc comments, `// OK: ...` on `unwrap*` calls.
- [Cycle protocol](../agent-data/cycle-protocol.md) and its act-time
  [checklists](../agent-data/cycle-checklists.md): cycle shape and numbering, per-commit
  flow, commit descriptions, pushing and close-out shapes.

==> /home/wink/data/prgs/rust/vc-x1-template/work/notes/done.md <==
# Done

As `../TODO.md` `## Done` sections fills move them to here.

See [Todo format](../AGENTS.md#todo-format)

==> /home/wink/data/prgs/rust/vc-x1-template/work/notes/dogfood.md <==
# Dogfood log

Dated entries on where the pinned instructions chafed, failed, or got amended; the evidence
base for proposing changes to the template repository. Newest first.

- <YYYY-MM-DD>: adopted at project creation via `vc-x1 init --use-template`

# vc-x1 config file

Configure the work-repo of a dual repo system. The other repo, we call the agent-repo, carries
its own markdown configuration file, typically also named .vc-config.md, with its own values.

The code blocks in these config files are in toml format and these blocks are logically
concatenated in the order written here and those become the information used for configuring
the system. The model for every table and key a workspace config may carry is
vc-config-model.md in the vc-x1 repo, generated from the schema.

The two repos
```toml
[repos]
work = "."
agent = ".claude"
```

## Bugs

1. Pool free-stack CAS is not cfg-gated: `src/pool.rs` calls `compare_exchange` unconditionally, so
   the whole crate fails to build on load/store-only targets (thumbv6m), contradicting the design's
   "the atomic floor rises only for pool users". The MPSC module gates on
   `target_has_atomic = "32"`, and pool (and registry, which uses Pool) should gate the same way.

# vc-x1 config file

This workspace's configuration. The `toml` fence below is the configuration itself, and the prose
around it is yours to write: only a fence tagged exactly `toml` is read.

Every settable key is documented in vc-x1's `vc-config.md`, and `vc-config-model.md` beside it
shows every table with its default or a typical value. `vc-x1 config` prints the same schema from
the binary you are running.

```toml
# vc-config: Vibe Coding workspace configuration
#
# [repos] is the workspace's repo registry: work and bot are paths
# relative to this file's directory (absolute allowed, discouraged).
# The entry that resolves to this config's own directory names the
# side: work = "." makes this the work repo.
#
# [remote] holds remote names rather than paths. agent-repo is the
# agent-repo's name on its remote, the last URL segment only, since
# the owner and the host come from the work repo's own remote.

[repos]
work = "."
agent = ".agent-session"

[remote]
agent-repo = "io_uring-2-zcr-v4-x1.agent-session"

# Optional keys: uncomment and edit to override the built-in
# default. `vc-x1 config` prints this list from the binary.

[agent-session]
# agent-session.items: Default agent-session item set (comma-separated)
#   used by: agent-session --<item> / --no-<item> / --all / --none
#   default: "headers,user,assistant,tool,summary"
#   reference: https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1/blob/HEAD/vc-config.md#agent-sessionitems
# items = "headers,user,assistant,tool,summary"

# agent-session.result-lines: Default --result-lines: max lines shown per tool result (0 =
#   unlimited)
#   used by: agent-session --result-lines
#   default: 10
#   reference: https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1/blob/HEAD/vc-config.md#agent-sessionresult-lines
# result-lines = 10

# agent-session.col-width: Default --col-width: first-column width in the --fields / --unknown /
#   --per-line views
#   used by: agent-session --col-width
#   default: 68
#   reference: https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1/blob/HEAD/vc-config.md#agent-sessioncol-width
# col-width = 68

[agent-files.diff]
# agent-files.diff.custom: Default for agent-files diff --custom: compare custom.md like the rest of
#   the set
#   used by: agent-files diff --custom
#   default: false
#   reference: https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1/blob/HEAD/vc-config.md#agent-filesdiffcustom
# custom = false

[agent-files.copy]
# agent-files.copy.custom: Default for agent-files copy --custom: copy custom.md with the rest of
#   the set
#   used by: agent-files copy --custom
#   default: false
#   reference: https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1/blob/HEAD/vc-config.md#agent-filescopycustom
# custom = false

[squash-push]
# squash-push.yes: Default for squash-push: act without asking once the precheck found work
#   used by: squash-push --yes / --ask
#   default: true
#   reference: https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1/blob/HEAD/vc-config.md#squash-pushyes
# yes = true

```

input.description: Read what squash-push does

content.content:
vc-x1 0.84.15

Squash SOURCE into TARGET (defaults: SOURCE=@, TARGET=@-),
advance a bookmark, and push.

Captures a repo's trailing working-copy writes into the last
commit and publishes it: rewriting an already-pushed commit,
so the push is a forced update. Built for the bot repo
(`.claude`, the session tail), and useful on the work repo as
a deliberate amend-and-push.

Zero-ceremony default: bare `vc-x1 squash-push` squashes
@ -> @- in `.` and pushes the bookmark of the line you are
on. With an empty `@` but work still to do, the squash is
skipped and the push still runs.

BOOKMARK defaults to the line's own bookmark, the nearest one
at or above the squash target, and there is no literal
default. On the agent repo that is `main`. On a work repo
running a cycle it is the topic bookmark, so a bare run
publishes the line you are working and never advances `main`.
Several candidates, or none, is an error asking you to name
one, since a wrong guess here publishes something.

A precheck asks whether the run has work at all: the working
copy at rest, the bookmark at its origin, and the bookmark
already at the squash target. That third condition is there
because a bookmark behind its target has a commit to publish
even when it matches origin. A run with no work prints
`<label>: clean` and exits 0 having touched nothing, <label>
being the repo's directory name. Every other run prints the
same line after the push, as a report only: the exit code
says whether the push completed, not what that line found.

With work found, the run acts without asking, the default
`squash-push.yes` sets. --ask turns the prompt on for one run
and -y/--yes turns it off. With the prompt on, a non-tty run
is an error rather than a hang, and declining is an error too.

As `vc-x1 push`'s squash-push-bot stage it says nothing and
asks nothing, there being no one mid-push to read a line or
answer a prompt. The precheck's decision still applies, so a
stage with no work still does nothing.

Usage: vc-x1 squash-push [OPTIONS] [BOOKMARK]

Arguments:
  [BOOKMARK]
          Bookmark to advance and push [default: the bookmark of the line you
          are on, the nearest one at or above the squash target]

Options:
  -R, --repo <REPO>
          Path to jj repo
          
          [default: .]

  -V, --version...
          Version detail on stdout: -V the banner, -VV the full report (as
          `vc-x1 version`). Counted like -v/-vv.
          
          Both ride along: they print, then the subcommand runs, so one
          invocation captures the version and the command's output together.
          That is why this replaces clap's auto-version, which would exit after
          printing. Without either, the banner still prints, on stderr.

      --no-banner
          Suppress the banner stderr normally carries on every run.
          
          Only the ambient banner: an explicit `-V` still prints, since asking
          for it outranks suppressing it.

      --squash [<SOURCE,TARGET>]
          Squash SOURCE into TARGET [default: @,@-]

      --allow-jj-mismatch
          Run even when `jj -V` disagrees with our linked jj-lib.
          
          Per-invocation on purpose, never a config key: a key gets set once
          during a frustrating afternoon and then silently protects nothing.

  -y, --yes
          Act without asking, once the precheck has found work

      --ask
          Ask before acting, overriding a configured squash-push.yes

  -v, --verbose...
          Verbose output: -v debug, -vv trace

      --log <LOG>
          Log file path (captures all levels)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

114-and body (`--yes` because push's gates need a tty the agent sandbox lacks, and the user's approval
115-of the shown title and body already covers them), stamps each new commit's `ochid:` trailer
116:([above](#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)), pushes the work bookmark, and squash-pushes the agent
117-repo's `main`. Three behaviors to keep in mind:
118-
119-- **No checks of the project's own.** vc-x1 runs no build or tests. Validation is the per-rung
120-  flow's job, run *before* the push. The one check that remains is `push-work` verifying the
121-  bookmark's remote refs are tracked.
122-- **Rerunning is safe.** Push keeps no state and cannot resume: every stage no-ops when its work is
123-  already done, so a failed run is re-run, not resumed. If push exits after `push-work` but before
124:  the agent-repo publish, `vc-x1 squash-push -R <agent-dir>` by hand is the rest of it.
125-- **`ochid:` trailers are stamped by push** ([No hand-written
126-  trailers](#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)), never hand-written into `--title` or `--body`.
127-- **The agent-repo is a linear journal.**
128-  - One push is one agent-repo commit on its `main`, paired with the work-repo commit, whatever
129-    bookmark the work-repo is on.
130-  - Never create an agent-repo bookmark mirroring a work-repo one: it steers session pushes at
131-    the wrong remote ref.
132:- **Squash-push again if `@` is non-empty** after a pass.
133-  - The agent keeps writing session data while the command runs, so its own record lands after
134-    the squash.
135-  - Session data is append-only, so a re-run never conflicts.
136-  - A single pass is never guaranteed to leave `@` empty.

## What a squash-push does here

`vc-x1 squash-push` in the work-repo folds the working copy into its parent and pushes that line's bookmark. Here the parent is `Initial commit` on `main`, which is already on GitHub. So:

- **The published `Initial commit` is rewritten** and `main` is force-pushed. On a repo this new, with nothing else built on it, I think that is the right shape: one setup commit rather than two.
- **The title stays `Initial commit`**, so my earlier title question goes away.
- **It bends two rules**: `main` advances only when a cycle lands, and a commit is made by `vc-x1 push`. You asked for squash-push by name, so I read that as the explicit exception, covering this one setup push and nothing after it. With no cycle open there is no cycle-record to note it in.

19 files, 2646 insertions:

Your approach is better than mine: the amend to `Initial commit` shrinks to the one line that was actually wrong, and the adoption becomes a real commit with its own description and `ochid:` trailers.

## How I'd do it

1. **Isolate the config change**: `jj new main`, then restore only `.vc-config.md` from the current change (`snxrmwrv`) into it. The new `@` holds the one-line rename and nothing else.
2. **Squash-push**: bare `vc-x1 squash-push` folds `@` into `Initial commit` and force-pushes `main`. The change id survives the squash, so any `ochid:` pointing at it stays valid.
3. **Return to the rest**: jj rebases `snxrmwrv` onto the rewritten `main` automatically and its `.vc-config.md` diff goes empty. I `jj edit` back to it and abandon the empty leftover.
4. **Push the adoption**: `vc-x1 push <bookmark> --title ... --body ...`, which also squash-pushes the agent-repo and stamps both trailers.

## Open points

- **Which bookmark for step 4**: I'd push straight to `main` as an explicit bootstrap exception. A single-step cycle wants a cycle-record, a version-of-record bump and a Land, and there is no manifest to bump yet. The alternative is a topic bookmark plus a fast-forward of `main`, which costs two more pushes and buys little here.
- **Validation**: `vc-x1 validate` still fails for lack of a `validate.full` table. `vc-x1 push` itself runs no checks, so this is only the agent-files' rule, and it needs your waiver for both pushes. If you would rather add a table, it belongs in the step 4 commit, not the squash.
- **Agent-repo config**: I have not read `.agent-session/.vc-config.md`. If it names the old repo, that should be fixed before step 4 so the paired commit carries it.
- **Title**: I'd suggest `chore: adopt agent-files v0.2.6`, with the body covering the `TODO.md` entry and the `notes/` skeleton. I'd still stop for "please review" and show you the description before pushing.
- **README title**: it reads `io_uring_2_zcr-v4`, which matches neither the old nor the new repo name. Step 4 is the cheap place to fix it if you want it changed.
- **Approvals**: there are two pushes, and each needs its own go, or one go that names both.

# Commit model

Two commit bodies from the `config loader` cycle in [cycle-model.md](cycle-model.md), shown as
specimens rather than a skeleton: a work rung's body and a bookend's. Copy the shape, not the
words. The rules are in [Commit-body form](prose.md#commit-body-form).

## A work rung

Title: `refactor: split loader from parser`

```
Config loading and parsing are one function, so the CLI cannot load a
config without parsing it and a test cannot parse one without a file on
disk. The move into its own module is what forces the split.

* The two jobs share one function and one error type.
  - `config::loader` finds and reads the file and returns the text with
    its path, so a caller that only wants to know which file was read
    stops there.
  - `config::parser` takes text and returns the schema, so a test hands
    it a string and never touches the filesystem.
* `main` still reaches into the parse result by field.
  - `main` calls `config::load` and receives the schema, so the field
    access moves behind the module boundary and the CLI no longer knows
    the file's shape.
```

The intro states this commit's problem and defines "split", the word the title assumes. Each `*`
is one facet of it, each `-` under a `*` answers that facet, and nothing names a file that the
diff already lists.

## A bookend

Title: `refactor: extract config loader opening`

```
Opens the cycle "refactor: extract config loader". Its record is the
In Progress block in TODO.md.
```

A bookend resolves no problem of its own, so its body is the intro paragraph alone, naming the
cycle by its title and pointing at its record. The closing's body is the same shape with "Closes".

vc-x1 0.84.15

Commit both repos, push the work repo's BOOKMARK, and
squash-push the bot repo's `main`: one command.

Collapses the manual commit-push-publish ceremony into a
single subcommand with two interactive approval gates.

Stages, in order:
  - review           approve the diff (first gate)
  - message          $EDITOR, or --title/--body; approve
                     the text (second gate). Skipped when
                     neither repo has pending changes
  - commit-work      commit the work repo. Skipped when
                     `@` is empty
  - commit-bot       commit `.claude`. Skipped when it is
                     clean
  - bookmark-set     work repo -> <bookmark>, bot -> main
  - push-work        publish <bookmark> to origin
  - squash-push-bot  fold `.claude`'s trailing writes
                     into its commit and push main

Rerunning is always safe: each stage does nothing when its
work is already done, so a failed run is re-run rather than
resumed. There is no saved state: vc-x1 cannot know why a
run failed, so it stops and reports. Please fix and try
again.

Failures in commit-work / commit-bot / bookmark-set roll both
repos back via `jj op restore` to a snapshot taken moments
earlier. Once push-work succeeds the work is published: from
there a change is either a new commit appended on top by the
next push, or an amend of what was pushed: `vc-x1
squash-push` folds the working copy into the last commit and
force-updates the remote.

vc-x1 runs no build or test steps: run your project's checks
yourself before pushing.

Non-interactive use: pass both --title and --body plus --yes
to skip both gates.

Usage: vc-x1 push [OPTIONS] [BOOKMARK]

Arguments:
  [BOOKMARK]
          Bookmark to advance in the work repo (positional form of
          `--bookmark`). The bot repo always advances `main`.
          
          Accepting a positional lets the common case read as `vc-x1 push main`
          without the `--bookmark` ceremony; `--bookmark` is kept as an alias
          for scripts and for composition with other args. The two forms
          conflict if both supplied.

Options:
      --bookmark <BOOKMARK>
          Bookmark to advance in the work repo (flag form, see positional)

  -V, --version...
          Version detail on stdout: -V the banner, -VV the full report (as
          `vc-x1 version`). Counted like -v/-vv.
          
          Both ride along: they print, then the subcommand runs, so one
          invocation captures the version and the command's output together.
          That is why this replaces clap's auto-version, which would exit after
          printing. Without either, the banner still prints, on stderr.

      --no-banner
          Suppress the banner stderr normally carries on every run.
          
          Only the ambient banner: an explicit `-V` still prints, since asking
          for it outranks suppressing it.

      --step
          Pause between every stage for an interactive approval gate

      --allow-jj-mismatch
          Run even when `jj -V` disagrees with our linked jj-lib.
          
          Per-invocation on purpose, never a config key: a key gets set once
          during a frustrating afternoon and then silently protects nothing.

      --no-squash-push
          Stop before `squash-push-bot` so it can be run manually

      --dry-run
          Print the exact commands for every stage without side effects

  -v, --verbose...
          Verbose output: -v debug, -vv trace

      --log <LOG>
          Log file path (captures all levels)

      --title <STR>
          Commit title (skip `$EDITOR` for the message stage)

      --body <STR>
          Commit body (skip `$EDITOR` for the message stage)

  -y, --yes
          Auto-approve interactive prompts (review gate, message-edit
          confirmation). Required when `--title` / `--body` aren't both supplied
          in non-interactive contexts

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

earlier. Once push-work succeeds the work is published: from
there a change is either a new commit appended on top by the
next push, or an amend of what was pushed: `vc-x1
squash-push` folds the working copy into the last commit and
force-updates the remote.

vc-x1 runs no build or test steps: run your project's checks
yourself before pushing.

Non-interactive use: pass both --title and --body plus --yes
to skip both gates.

Usage: vc-x1 push [OPTIONS] [BOOKMARK]

Arguments:
  [BOOKMARK]
          Bookmark to advance in the work repo (positional form of
          `--bookmark`). The bot repo always advances `main`.
          
          Accepting a positional lets the common case read as `vc-x1 push main`
          without the `--bookmark` ceremony; `--bookmark` is kept as an alias
          for scripts and for composition with other args. The two forms
          conflict if both supplied.

Options:
      --bookmark <BOOKMARK>
          Bookmark to advance in the work repo (flag form, see positional)

  -V, --version...
          Version detail on stdout: -V the banner, -VV the full report (as
          `vc-x1 version`). Counted like -v/-vv.
          
          Both ride along: they print, then the subcommand runs, so one
          invocation captures the version and the command's output together.
          That is why this replaces clap's auto-version, which would exit after
          printing. Without either, the banner still prints, on stderr.

      --no-banner
          Suppress the banner stderr normally carries on every run.
          
          Only the ambient banner: an explicit `-V` still prints, since asking
          for it outranks suppressing it.

      --step
          Pause between every stage for an interactive approval gate

      --allow-jj-mismatch
          Run even when `jj -V` disagrees with our linked jj-lib.
          
          Per-invocation on purpose, never a config key: a key gets set once
          during a frustrating afternoon and then silently protects nothing.

      --no-squash-push
          Stop before `squash-push-bot` so it can be run manually

      --dry-run
          Print the exact commands for every stage without side effects

  -v, --verbose...
          Verbose output: -v debug, -vv trace

      --log <LOG>
          Log file path (captures all levels)

      --title <STR>
          Commit title (skip `$EDITOR` for the message stage)

      --body <STR>
          Commit body (skip `$EDITOR` for the message stage)

  -y, --yes
          Auto-approve interactive prompts (review gate, message-edit
          confirmation). Required when `--title` / `--body` aren't both supplied
          in non-interactive contexts

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

257

259	  reference-linked to the rung's subsection via `[M]: #<slug>` in the file's `# References` (the
260	  closing rung linked like the rest), and the `(current)` / `(done)` marker. Its position in the
261	  list is its position in the ladder. The last rung is the close-out and its text says so. Detail
262	  lives not on the rung but in its subsection under the ladder, headed by the rung's exact
263	  title (see the protocol's [Opening](../AGENTS.md#opening)), bulleted, never `;`-joined inline.
264	- **Commit description**: no prefix. The title is the first line, and the body is the prose (see
265	  [Commit description](../AGENTS.md#commit-description)).
266	
267	The title is **identical** across both for a given step, so a step's ladder entry and its commit
268	title line up verbatim. The rung's subsection heading carries the same title, a third
269	surface on every rung (the closing rung's exists only when close-out gotchas occurred: see the

271

273	title, never one shared cycle title uniquified by a step marker. The block's title heading carries
274	the *cycle title*, the bare name no multi-step commit carries (see the bookends below). To keep a
275	cycle's commits collectable with one `git log --grep`, give the step titles a common greppable stem
276	(e.g. `config loader`).
277	
278	**Cycle bookend titles**: a multi-step cycle's bookend commits are the cycle title plus a suffix, "
279	opening" and " closing", same type (`feat: dynamic warmup opening` /
280	`feat: dynamic warmup closing`), so one `git log --grep "<cycle title>"` returns the pair that
281	brackets the ladder. The bare cycle title is the cycle's *name*: the block's title heading carries
282	it, and no multi-step commit does, which is also what keeps the closing rung's subsection anchor
283	clear of the title heading's. A single-step cycle's one commit is the cycle and keeps the bare

The config rename is squashed into `Initial commit` and pushed to `main` (now `b10ad189`). The working copy is back on the adoption change, holding the other 18 files, and the agent-repo config needed no fix.

Here is the description for the second push. The agent-files declare their own title type for this, so I used it instead of the `chore:` I suggested earlier.

Title:

```
agent-files(adoption): v0.2.6
```

Body:

```
The repo holds only what `vc-x1 init` wrote, so an agent starting here
has no rules to follow and no record of the work to be done. Adoption
is copying the agent-files set from its source as this project's own.

* No rules govern how an agent works here.
  - The agent-files set is copied in whole, and `custom.md` points at
    the shared messages repo, whose README is the protocol.
* The project's work has nowhere to be recorded.
  - `TODO.md` takes the set's skeleton and one entry, the app that
    reads keyboard bytes through io_uring.
  - `notes/` opens with the backlog and the bug list the skeleton
    links to.
* The repo does not say what it is or how it is licensed.
  - A README states the aim, and the two licenses it offers sit
    beside it.
